ai.description: This legless lizard reaches 15 cm. It is uniform dark brown with a blunt, rounded head and tail. It lacks external limbs and visible ear openings, resembling a large, smooth-scaled earthworm.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dibamus nicobaricum* is distinguished from other Indian squamates by its completely limbless, worm-like body and the presence of a single, large, undivided rostral scale.
ai.habitat: *Dibamus nicobaricum* inhabits the moist tropical forests of the Nicobar Islands, typically found burrowing in leaf litter or decaying logs within lowland areas.
ai.behavior: The Nicobar worm lizard is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates within the leaf litter and soil of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dibamus nicobaricum* is oviparous, laying a single-egg clutch. While specific breeding seasons remain poorly documented, they likely reproduce during the monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dibamus nicobaricum* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring at low elevations within this tropical island biogeographic zone.
